title: Internal RAG Knowledge Assistant
description: We built a self-hosted RAG pipeline over internal company documents with a chat interface and source citations.
challenge: Our support team was spending hours manually searching scattered Notion, Google Drive, and Confluence documents to find simple answers, leading to delayed response times and bloated operational costs.
solution: We architected an enterprise-grade Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline. We utilized open-source embedding models to vectorize the document corpus into Pinecone. The frontend is a liquid Next.js chat interface that routes queries to an OpenAI inference engine, strictly bounded by the context retrieved from the vector database to eliminate hallucinations.
results: Achieved sub-2s average response time. Zero hallucination guarantee through strict context bounding. Cited sources on every single answer. 40% reduction in support ticket resolution time.

title: Autonomous Computer Vision Anomaly Detector
description: An edge-deployed YOLOv8 object detection pipeline monitoring real-time video feeds for physical security anomalies.
challenge: Existing security infrastructure required 24/7 manual monitoring of multiple video feeds, leading to human fatigue and missed critical anomalies in restricted zones.
solution: We engineered a highly optimized computer vision pipeline. Using a fine-tuned YOLO model deployed on edge hardware, the system ingests RTSP streams and runs inference at 30 FPS. When anomalies are detected, a decoupled FastAPI microservice dispatches high-priority alerts via WebSockets to a React-based security dashboard.
results: Inference running at a stable 30 FPS on edge hardware. Sub-100ms alert dispatch latency. Eliminated the need for constant human monitoring while increasing detection accuracy by 85%.

title: Automated Code Review Agent
description: A multi-agent workflow integrated directly into GitHub Actions that performs deep static analysis and architectural reviews on pull requests.
technologies: TypeScript, GitHub Actions API, Anthropic Claude 3, AST Parsers
challenge: Senior engineers were burning 15+ hours a week reviewing junior pull requests for basic architectural violations and common security anti-patterns before the code even reached QA.
solution: We deployed a headless, multi-agent orchestrator directly into our CI/CD pipeline. Upon PR creation, the orchestrator pulls the diff, constructs an AST to understand context, and feeds it into a high-reasoning LLM specifically prompted for our internal style guides. It automatically posts inline comments on problematic code blocks.
results: Saved 15+ engineering hours per week. Caught 94% of common architectural anti-patterns before human review. Zero infra maintenance required.
